lines: This is how a Popkin starts.
A name, a code, and a QR code for everyone you want in.
First, say what to call you, and add a phone number or an email.
There is no password to make up.
We send you six digits.
Type them in and you are signed in, for thirty days.
Open it on something wider and the screen splits in two.
The form on one side, a picture on the other.
Now name your Popkin, and pick an emoji and a colour.
The card beside the form shows how it will look to everyone, and follows every choice.
Choose how long it lasts: just today, the weekend, until a date, or keep it going.
You can change it later.
Pop it up.
There is the QR code to hold up, and the invite link to copy, text or share.
You are its Host, and its first member.
It works by touch on a phone and by keyboard on a desktop, in light and in dark.
What no screen shows, the tests prove.
Codes are stored hashed, expire after ten minutes, and work only once.
One thing is left for the owner: choosing who sends the texts and the emails.
Until then, the code goes to the log.
That is journey one. Popkin is a free platform for pop-up communities.
